newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields dive on Fed restraint.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields dive on Fed restraint.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell heavily on Wednesday as the debt market celebrated the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision not to cut key rates on Tuesday.
An unexpected fall in August producer prices also helped the buoyant mood of the market. The August PPI index fell 0.4 percent, against market expectations of a 0.1 percent rise.
Nine-year bond yields fell all of 17 basis points to 7.48 percent, whilst the six-month T-bill rate dipped six basis points to 4.72 percent.

The crown appreciated against the mark in the morning session, but fell below Tuesday's afternoon fix levels after the Riksbank announced it could intervene on the currency markets to stabilise the value of the crown.
However, the Riksbank emphasised that it would not aim to defend a pre-set level, and said the move was not intended as a precursor to ERM membership.
"Our initial interpretation is that the crown has now reached a peak that the Riksbank wants to defend," one analyst said. Others said the policy matched that in other European countries.
The crown eased to 4.3635 against the mark compared with a level of 4.3520 Tuesday afternoon.
